policy: First release or public introduction, including early previews. Mech uses 2026 for the benchmark version under test, as requested, rather than its historical introduction year. Runtime variants inherit their language's year; dates and their basis are recorded individually.

c.name: C
c.note: Conventional introduction year; Ritchie dates C's most formative period to 1972.

matlab.name: MATLAB
matlab.note: PC-MATLAB debuted publicly in December 1984; earlier academic matrix-calculator development is excluded.

lisp.name: Common Lisp
lisp.note: Common Lisp: The Language first edition was published in 1984 and became the de facto standard; this comparison uses the Common Lisp family implemented by SBCL, not the earlier Lisp lineage.

cpp.name: C++
cpp.note: First commercial implementation in October 1985; earlier C with Classes work is excluded.

haskell.name: Haskell
haskell.note: Haskell 1.0 report released on April 1, 1990, per the language designers' history.

erlang.name: Erlang
erlang.note: Presented publicly at ISS'90, followed by a fast implementation release to users in 1991. Uses the existing public-introduction policy; earlier internal experimentation is excluded.

lua.name: Lua
lua.note: Public introduction in 1993; first downloadable release followed in 1994. LuaJIT uses Lua's year.

k.name: K
k.note: First K version supplied commercially in 1993; Growler uses K's year.

java.name: Java
java.note: Java's public debut in 1995; later JVM and AOT releases share this language year.

php.name: PHP
php.note: PHP Tools source released publicly in June 1995.

racket.name: Racket
racket.note: First public MzScheme release in September 1995. The PLT Scheme family was renamed Racket in 2010; this uses the earliest public family year.

ocaml.name: OCaml
ocaml.note: Objective Caml was released in 1996; the official name became OCaml in 2011.

chapel.name: Chapel
chapel.note: First public release, v0.8, in November 2008, per Chapel's release timeline.

go.name: Go
go.note: First open-source public release in November 2009.

rust.name: Rust
rust.note: Public introduction in July 2010; numbered 0.1 and stable 1.0 releases followed in 2012 and 2015.

swift.name: Swift
swift.note: Public beta introduced on June 2, 2014, with Apple's iOS 8 SDK.

futhark.name: Futhark
futhark.note: First compiler release, 0.1.0, on October 4, 2017; earlier research development is excluded.

mech.name: Mech
mech.note: 2026 benchmark development version under test, per the requested comparison policy. AOT, JIT, and interpreted modes share this year; it is not a claim about Mech's first public introduction.

bqn.name: BQN
bqn.note: Public development and introduction in 2020; CBQN uses BQN's year.

zig.name: Zig
zig.note: Public introduction in February 2016 in the creator’s introduction to Zig.

odin.name: Odin
odin.note: Public development began in July 2016, per the official language FAQ.

roc.name: Roc
roc.note: Uses 2020 for its early public development and introduction, consistent with the creator’s 2020 guide. Earlier internal design is excluded; Roc has not released a stable 0.1. The measured compiler is the established alpha4 LLVM release from September 2025.

elm.name: Elm
elm.note: Initial public release 0.1 in April 2012, per the official release history.

csharp.name: C#
csharp.note: Microsoft publicly introduced C# on June 26, 2000, with an early technical preview announced for July.

fsharp.name: F#
fsharp.note: Don Syme dates the first public F# v0.1 release to June 4, 2002 in his language history, page 19.

ada.name: Ada
ada.note: Conventional first-release year, Ada 80; the later Ada 83 standard is not used as the introduction date.

pascal.name: Pascal
pascal.note: Niklaus Wirth records Pascal publication in 1970. This benchmark uses Free Pascal; its compiler release year does not replace the language year.

fortran.name: Fortran
fortran.note: IBM records the commercial release of Fortran and its first compiler in 1957.

dart.name: Dart
dart.note: Google publicly introduced Dart on October 10, 2011; AOT and JIT variants inherit this year.

smalltalk.name: Smalltalk
smalltalk.note: Smalltalk-72 first appeared in 1972, according to the Computer History Museum archive with Dan Ingalls. The current benchmark uses Pharo.

d.name: D
d.note: First public DMD alpha release in December 2001, as recorded by Walter Bright. The LDC compiler version does not replace the language introduction year.
